drawn_from: 40 of the 613 matches, 10 label findings and all 12 duplicate findings of the 556 check

cases.note: Status is right via C1091 (historical direction, Deut 20:1–4), but S116 is a topical study and should not be listed as itemizing.
cases.action: Removed S116 from N58; its status (only a historical direction, C1091) stands.

cases.note: S126 is a topical study. C0655 (Torah Law, Lev 21:5) states the same mourning-baldness ban, which Maimonides counts once, so torah_law.
cases.action: Corrected: N171 is itemized by C0655 at the 556 and now also by S126, which the revision made Torah Law.

cases.note: S134 is a topical study and cannot itemize. C0230 (Torah Law, pilgrim feasts at Ex 23:14, Maimonides' own P53 verse) covers it: torah_law.
cases.action: Corrected: P53 is itemized by C0230 at the 556; the revision has since added Exodus 23:17 to C0230.

cases.note: The conflict with C0418 is real, but C0800 is itself a ban, not a positive half; twin C0801 (frankincense) needs the same fix.
cases.action: Regrouped C0800 and C0801 as 'same ban under two labels' beside C0418, which now holds both bans.

cases.note: Defensible as a standing priestly duty, but the comparators are selective: lamps C0284, incense C0337 and daily offering C0333 were also Instruction.
cases.action: Kept, with new evidence: the revision has since made the lamps (C0284), incense (C0337) and daily offering (C0333) Torah Law, so the priestly blessing is now the odd one out.

cases.note: C0129 and AUD-02-31-13 restate it, but C0152 (the work ban, Decalogue Command) is a separate clause. Ex 31:13–17 is arguably the better anchor.
cases.action: Narrowed to C0129 and AUD-02-31-13. The revision keeps the holy-day command and the covenant sign apart on purpose, so this is left as a choice and not counted.

summary: 56 were correct, 4 partly right and 2 wrong. The two wrong ones (N171, P53) were commandments the 556 check had treated as held only by topical studies; C0655 and C0230 do state them. Both are corrected here, and the partly right ones are narrowed or re-evidenced.
